subject: Private VPC — edge fabric demarcation & control/data interface review
messages:
From: CoreBank Network Team <networking@corebank.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@corebank.com, alice.morgan@corebank.com
Date: Mon, 4 Jan 2027 13:12:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Private deployment review request — edge attachment details

Rishi,

Thanks again for taking this on. We ran an internal review and surfaced a few open questions on how Redwood expects the edge fabric to be demarcated from our internal network for the control plane vs data plane. The main items:

- Where will the control plane egress originate (management plane vs customer control plane)?
- Expected IP ranges and NATing behavior for model-serving data plane egress (we have strict outbound ACLs).
- TLS termination expectations across the demarc (mTLS between pods? TLS passthrough?).
- Audit log / flow log collection points we should expose to meet our compliance audit.

We have a kickoff with our security and network teams Wednesday; it would be helpful to have a single-page reference diagram and a short runbook we can review.

Can you share the latest diagram and a short checklist (routing, ports, cert rotation notes) by EOD tomorrow? We attached our internal network boundary policy for reference.

Thanks,
Alice Morgan
Head of Cloud Ops — CoreBank
[Attachment: corebank-boundary-policy.pdf]

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Private deployment review request — edge attachment details

Alice / CoreBank team,

Appreciate the note and the policy doc — good context. I attached a concise reference pack that should cover each ask:

- redwood-ref-diagram-vpc.png: single-pane view of control plane (management/control API) vs data plane (inference traffic) demarc, including recommended NAT and peering points.
- edge-demarcation-v3.pdf: short playbook — recommended routing, port matrix, and cert responsibilities.
- control-data-interface-matrix.csv: explicit source/destination combos we typically observe.

Quick answers in-line to your bullets:
1) Control plane egress: outbound control calls originate from the private control plane proxies (customer-owned control plane in Private deployments). By default we recommend routing control-plane control to the management subnet over a direct peering (no SNAT) so you see source IPs. If you require outbound egress through your gateway, we can support SNAT but will mark audit log entries accordingly.

2) Data plane NATing: We recommend no SNAT for inference egress where possible; if your internal policy mandates SNAT, we'll provide predictable ephemeral IP pools and annotate them in the matrix. We also include an optional egress-proxy sidecar pattern in the playbook.

3) TLS termination: Our standard is end-to-end TLS with mutual TLS for control-plane calls (Redwood client proxies <-> customer control plane). For model-serving data plane, we support TLS passthrough to customer-provided ingress certificates or Redwood-managed certs depending on your compliance needs. Details in the playbook section 2.

4) Audit/flow logs: We expose flow logs at the demarc and emit S3/Cloud storage-compatible artifacts; the playbook also outlines hooks for pulling vpc_flow logs into your SIEM and adding our runtime audit keys.

Can we do a 30m sync tomorrow at 10:00 CET with your security lead to walk through the diagram? If that works I'll send a calendar invite and a short agenda.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-ref-diagram-vpc.png] [Attachment: edge-demarcation-v3.pdf]

From: irene_choi@redwood.ai

Rishi — quick review notes from the security perspective before the sync:

- Please ensure the diagram explicitly marks which control-plane endpoints are customer-owned vs Redwood-managed. We had feedback in previous deployments where customers assumed Redwood rotated control-plane certs; clarify responsibility.
- Add an optional flow showing the egress-proxy sidecar (explicitly call out health-check ports 8081/8443) — some auditors require service-level probes be visible.
- For the audit logs, include our recommended retention defaults (90d warm, 365d cold) and a sample S3 prefix example so customers can validate lifecycle policies.
- Call out the failover behavior if the peering is temporarily unavailable (route to fallback region or restricted degraded mode).

I'll attach a slightly redlined copy after I run it by Kim. Also flagging JIRA-ITINFRA-789 as an item to track any IP-allocation requests from CoreBank.

Thanks — I can join the 10:00 CET slot and will bring the compliance checklist.

— Irene
Principal Security Engineer — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: control-data-interface-matrix.csv]

Alice / team — thanks for the detailed ask and thanks Rishi/Irene for the quick turnaround. Confirming a few operational and compliance items ahead of tomorrow's call:

- We will bring a one-page responsibilities matrix to the call that maps: cert lifecycle (who rotates), log retention responsibilities, and where to validate token/key revocation.
- For SOC 2 evidence, we will provide the last 3 months of control-plane connection logs and a sample of flow logs (redacted) during your audit window. We'll need a signed data request form from your security team to share the artifacts.
- If CoreBank requires forced SNAT for outbound inference traffic, expect a 48–72h window to provision static egress allocation in our staging pool and update the runbook accordingly.

Agenda I propose for the 30m tomorrow:
1) Walk the diagram (5m)
2) Clarify cert and key responsibilities (7m)
3) Validate egress behavior and IP allocation options (10m)
4) Action items & evidence request next steps (8m)

Rishi — please send the invite; Alice — thanks, please include the security contact and the SOC lead so we can align evidence scoping.

Kimberly Park
Director, Trust & Security — Redwood Inference
